facts.claim: Backpropagation was popularised in 1986 by Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams, 'Learning representations by back-propagating errors', Nature 323, 533-536.
Anthropic's 'Towards Monosemanticity' (published Oct 4, 2023) used a sparse autoencoder to extract a large number of interpretable features from a one-layer transformer.

Epoch AI's database rows (re-checked 2026-10-10): GPT-3 5.10 MW x 355.2 h = 1.81 GWh; GPT-4 19.9 MW x 2,280 h = 45.5 GWh; Grok 3 110 MW x 2,160 h = 237.5 GWh; GPT-6 Astra 232.7 MW x 2,160 h (Epoch's 90-day assumption) = 502.6 GWh. Astra / GPT-3 = about 280 times (our arithmetic on Epoch estimates).
facts.source: Epoch AI all_ai_models.csv (subset saved as epoch-all-ai-models-subset.csv)

facts.claim: Epoch AI's GPT-6 Astra note: '~100k GB200s over 90 days at 25% FP8 MFU' gives around 1e27 FLOP; OpenAI has not disclosed the training duration or energy.
GPT-6 Astra used about 3,000 times GPT-3's training compute (1.0e27 vs 3.14e23 FLOP) and about 2 billion times AlexNet's (4.7e17 FLOP), per Epoch AI estimates (our division).
